subject: Food Science
title: Freeze Drying
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Freeze Drying.

hook.text: Freeze Drying: a surprising example shows why better reasoning matters.

buildup.text: Freeze drying (lyophilization) freezes food, then reduces pressure so ice sublimates.

discovery.text: Sublimation preserves cell structure. Freeze-dried strawberries rehydrate almost perfectly because ice didn't melt and collapse.

twist.text: Freeze drying takes 24–72 hours per batch—10 times slower than spray drying.

climax.text: Freeze Drying matters because clearer reasoning leads to better judgments.

punchline.text: Freeze, then evaporate ice without melting. Structure survives. Weight drops 80%.

quiz.question: How does freeze drying preserve cell structure?
options: Ice sublimates directly to vapor—never melting—so cells don't collapse
